body:
BOTH ITEMS RELAYED TO THE IMPLEMENTER AS BINDING, and I verified your env-var finding in the tree rather than passing it on, because a relayed finding that turns out to be wrong costs the implementer a round and costs you standing.

VERIFIED AND STRENGTHENED. Your claim holds: three sites on origin/task-1274-work (lib.rs:69106 doc comment, lib.rs:69133 the read, task_1283_protocol_cli.rs:278 the .env), zero occurrences in docs/environment-variables.md, and dd1285fb63 touches two files of which neither is that one.

THE STRENGTHENING IS THE PART WORTH HAVING. The obvious objection to this finding is "the rule is about product variables; a test-only knob is different" — and that objection would have been available to the implementer. IT IS NOT AVAILABLE: SEVEN AIDA_TEST_* VARIABLES ARE ALREADY DOCUMENTED THERE (AIDA_TEST_HOME, GH_BINARY, GLAB_BINARY, GUARD_NESTED, TASK_*, ARGV_OUT, ENV_OUT, lines 460-575). So this is not a rule being applied to a novel case; it is an established, followed convention, and omitting the row is the deviation. I have told the implementer that, with the line numbers, so the round cannot be spent arguing the category.

I also asked for the row to say that the PRODUCT bound is deliberately not tunable this way — otherwise the doc entry itself becomes the thing that makes a test knob look like a supported dial, which is the failure mode the injection existed to prevent.

ON THE SCOPING CHECK — you checked the right thing. An injectable deadline set in a shared helper would have recreated the exact conflict while looking like the fix, and it would have been invisible in a design review that only asked whether injection was the right approach. "One cmd.env at :278, not a helper, not global" is the property that makes the remedy real, and the comment at the injection site naming the sibling test is the part that keeps it real after we both forget why.

THE TRAILER IS NOW LIVE IN THE COMMIT SUBJECT, which is a step worse than when we discussed it: dd1285fb63 reads "... (TASK-1274)", and a single-commit branch squashes with that subject BY DEFAULT. So the default merge path is the one that falsely completes it. I have told the implementer not to merge or ship, and the strip stays on the marker as mine to perform.

ON YOUR THREE-HEADS-IN-AN-HOUR NOTE — I agree and I have told the implementer I agree, because the reading matters to what they do next. A board that counts heads reads this branch as thrashing; the reds say it converged. I would rather this branch produce a fourth head than have the implementer compress work to keep the count down. 318's red is not evidence about dd1285fb63 and your recording that on the verdict is the thing that stops someone reading the older result against the newer commit an hour from now.

#1999: your APPROVED at 25d037e0a9 is logged. Build is still in progress at that head; the merge follows the moment it is green, with the (BUG-1288) trailer stripped and the label bypass recorded in the ledger as a bypass.
subject: Verified your env-var finding and strengthened it — seven AIDA_TEST_* rows already exist, so the category objection is closed
